pr_body:
The COMPAT locale data provider has been removed in JDK23 by https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/pull/17991. This PR swaps out the old COMPAT locale provider for the default CLDR provider.

As part of this, the differences between CLDR and COMPAT have been encapsulated by the `CompatCalendarNameProvider` class, generated manually (for now) between two diffs of the contents of each locale provider, as given in the javadoc. This is applied by the SPI locale provider, before CLDR is queried.

Although the JDK may have changed the locale behaviour, we still need to maintain the existing behaviour for our customers across minor versions. We can't just change how date formats work in a minor ES release, despite them all actually coming from the JDK - they should work the same regardless of the JDK version that ES runs on.

Deprecation and migration strategies for ESv9+ are still to be determined.

This fixes #109003
pr_title: Change COMPAT locale references to CLDR
pr_comment: Hi @thecoop, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

This actually has quite a significant difference - the ROOT locale differs in behaviour between COMPAT and CLDR; one such difference is that it doesn't have long day/month names, only short names, which given we use ROOT for everything has a significant impact on our date formatters

eg `EEEE, MMMM dd, yyyy` outputs `Monday, January 01, 2024` under ROOT COMPAT, but `Mon, Jan 01, 2024` under ROOT CLDR. This is [by design](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8233701), and due to the ROOT locale being as language-agnostic as possible.
Does this change need to be conditional based on the runtime JVM or is it safe to just change it for all supported runtimes?
It can be made generally, as the CLDR provider is present in earlier JVMs, just that the COMPAT locale has been removed

There's also differences in german between COMPAT and CLDR. `E` day-of-week format produces `Mo` on COMPAT and `Mo.` on CLDR. This changes parsing and outputting of dates using that specifier. How are we going to find all of these differences, short of replicating the entirety of COMPAT in the ES codebase?

> short of replicating the entirety of COMPAT in the ES codebase?

I think that is the only way to maintain the COMPAT behavior until we can properly deprecate the behavior.
can we copy the entire compat locale providers into a small jar that we include as a dependency (and use with SPI) and remove at some point in the future?

The PR that removed COMPAT is https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/pull/17991, it covers over 500 files. I'm also not clear where the ROOT locale information is stored - I can't find it in the various removed files.
